east_10th_verdict: NOT SUPPORTED, and contradicted for 1934-1947. It remains OPEN for roughly 1923-1934. Reasons: (1) Every Erie Indian dealer address found on a primary page image is somewhere other than East 10th. LeJeal Cycle Works was at 1721 Sassafras (1908 to about 1922). A. D. Beckman was at 1807 Parade (Nov-Dec 1922). The 'Indian Motorcycle Agency' was at 120 E 11th, phone 69-312 (Jul 1935, Jan 1936, Jul 1936), then at 302 E 11th, phone 48-385 (Jul 1937, the same address and phone as 'Bayhurst Charles motorcycles'). I viewed the 1935 and 1937 crops myself. (2) The Motorcycles heading in all 16 LOC phone books from 1934 to 1947 was read on the images; it never lists an East 10th shop. The wider finding of no motorcycle or bicycle business on E 10th from 1911 to 1947 is OCR-only. (3) In the Aug 1939 Atkinson directory, the 'Motorcycle Dealers' heading names two dealers, both on E 11th (114 and 302), but this is a snippet only. (4) The 1950 Sanborn shows no motorcycle shop on the E 10th 100 block; the 200-400 blocks were not fully checked. Why it stays open: no Erie directory or phone book for 1915-1933 could be reached; the Indian dealer for about 1923-1934 is unidentified (Beckman may have left the trade by 1927); and Bayhurst's 1930 'Owner, Bicycles' business has no known address. Best reconciliation (interpretation, not proven): the 1935-36 agency at 120 E 11th, and the Harley shop at 114, stood on the north side of E 11th, on the same city block as the E 10th auto row. On the 1950 Sanborn, the 118-120 E 11th building backs directly onto the 117-129 E 10th garage at mid-block. In the 1937-47 phone books, one firm (Moorhouse) held 118 E 11th and later 117 E 10th. So the shop sat on 'the Tenth Street block', and a 10th/11th mix-up, or a rear entrance on E 10th, is plausible. Minor alternative: a Goodyear tire store at 163 E 10th also sold bicycles in 1939 (snippet only).
